business_definition: Unique identifier for each member/policyholder. Surrogate key assigned at enrollment.
Code identifying the health plan the member is enrolled in (e.g. MCR-STD or MCD-STD or PRV-SLVR).
Broad insurance category: Medicare or Medicaid or Private or Self-Pay.
Two-letter US state code representing the member geographic region.
Date the member enrolled in their current health plan (MM/DD/YYYY).
Current enrollment status of the member: Active or Terminated.
Standardized procedure or diagnosis code (CPT or ICD-10). Primary identifier for this catalog entry.
Classification of the code: Procedure (CPT) or Diagnosis (ICD-10).
Human-readable description of the procedure or diagnosis associated with the code.
Clinical or administrative grouping for the code (e.g. Evaluation & Management or Laboratory or Physical Therapy).
Indicator (Y/N) of whether this code requires manual clinical review before a coverage decision.
Unique identifier for each submitted claim event. Surrogate key assigned at submission.
References the member who received the service. Links to patient_accounts.member_id.
Identifier for the healthcare provider who rendered the service.
Health plan code active for the member at time of service. Links to patient_accounts.plan_code.
Insurance category for the claim. Denormalized from patient_accounts for audit traceability.
ICD-10 diagnosis code recorded on the claim. Links to procedure_catalog.code for review rules.
CPT procedure code billed on the claim. Links to procedure_catalog.code for coverage and review rules.
Total dollar amount billed by the provider for the service.
Dollar amount approved by the payer under the applicable plan policy.
Date the medical service was rendered (MM/DD/YYYY). Key field for point-in-time policy matching.
Date the claim was submitted to the payer (MM/DD/YYYY).
Payer decision on the claim: Approved or Denied or Pending.
Two-letter US state where the patient received care. Used for regional compliance analysis.
Age of the patient at the time of service in years.
Reported gender of the patient: Male or Female.
Clinical specialty of the rendering provider (e.g. Cardiology or General Practice). May be null if not reported.
Classification of the encounter: Outpatient or Inpatient or Emergency.
Number of inpatient days. Zero for outpatient and emergency visits.
Indicates (1/0) whether the patient has a documented chronic condition relevant to the claim.
Number of visits by this member in the prior 12 months. May be null for new members.
Calculated lag in days between date_of_service and submission_date. Used in timeliness and fraud analysis.
Rolling monthly claim count for the rendering provider. Used as a fraud/volume indicator.
Controlled quality flag (1/0) indicating a claim marked for potential fraud review. Intentional governance test field.
